actions.action: Check whether the soil is bone-dry and the pot feels light within a day or two of watering
Monitor whether yellowing spreads beyond the older lower leaves
Repot into a pot about 2 inches wider with regular potting mix and about 25% perlite, shaking off the old soil
Pull unwanted stowaway plants with their roots
Water thoroughly when the top inch of soil is dry, until it drains from the bottom
Feed a balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength every 2-3 weeks through summer
Snip seed stalks once the flowers fade

reason: The answer calls the plant mostly healthy but 'a bit hungry,' puts nutrient shortage as a secondary possibility and hedges on the Kalanchoe, so the diagnosis is partial; its first fix, repotting into a less fast-draining mix, matches what worked, and nothing it suggests is harmful.
